rules.title: Type-stable hot functions
rules.what: Keep hot functions type-stable: pass values as arguments or declare true constants const; check with @code_warntype before optimising anything else.
rules.why: A non-constant global has no fixed type, so the compiler cannot specialise the functions that read it and boxes every value, at every call.
rules.how: const RATE = 0.2; function f(x, rate) ... end; @code_warntype f(x, rate); BenchmarkTools for timing.

patterns.note: Global mutated from a function; type instability candidate.

verify.how: @code_warntype clean on the hot function; @btime before/after.

rules.title: Preallocate and reuse buffers
rules.what: Preallocate arrays whose size is known (sizehint!, Vector{T}(undef, n)) and mutate in place instead of growing with push! in loops.
rules.why: Repeated push! reallocates and copies as the array doubles; when the final size is known that work is avoidable.
rules.how: out = Vector{Float64}(undef, n); or sizehint!(out, n); reuse buffers across iterations with in-place (!) functions.

patterns.note: Array grown by push!; fine when the size is unknown.

verify.how: @allocated or @btime shows fewer allocations on the hot loop.

rules.title: Bounded threads, measured after warm-up
rules.what: Measure the sequential version first, then size threading to the work per item and the cores the machine can spare; compare after compilation and warm-up; precompile stable workloads.
rules.why: @threads takes every core the runtime was given; on a shared machine it takes them from other work, for a gain that depends on the work per item.
rules.how: julia -t N with N chosen from measurement; PrecompileTools for long-running services; compare steady-state timings.

patterns.note: Threading; check it is measured and bounded.

verify.how: Sequential and threaded timings after warm-up recorded together.
